name: sendto
synopsis: ssize_t sendto(int sockfd, const void *buf[.len], size_t len, int flags, const struct sockaddr *dest_addr, socklen_t addrlen);
description: The sendto() system call transmits a message to another socket, specifying the destination address. It can be used on both connected and unconnected sockets, but for connected sockets, the destination is ignored and may return an error.

parameters.name: sockfd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the socket to send from

parameters.name: buf
parameters.description: Buffer containing the message to send

parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Length of the message in bytes

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Bitwise OR of flags to modify behavior, such as MSG_CONFIRM or MSG_DONTROUTE

parameters.name: dest_addr
parameters.description: Pointer to the destination address structure

parameters.name: addrlen
parameters.description: Length of the destination address structure

return_value.success: Returns the number of bytes sent
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: Write permission denied on the destination or invalid broadcast attempt
Nonblocking socket would block, or no ephemeral port available
Another Fast Open is in progress
sockfd is not a valid file descriptor
No peer address is set for a non-connection-mode socket
An invalid user space address was specified
A signal occurred before data was transmitted
Socket is already connected and a recipient was specified
Message too long to send atomically
No buffer space available for sending
Socket is not connected and no target is given
sockfd does not refer to a socket
A flag is inappropriate for the socket type
Local end has been shut down on a connection-oriented socket

bugs: Linux may return EPIPE instead of ENOTCONN.
